blocks.observation: Section heading for the Qur'an passages; current text opens "## What the Qur'an Establishes".
blocks.text: ## What the Qur'an Establishes

blocks.observation: Scope limit that 3:169 neither grants every-martyr hearing nor describes the body; current text opens "It does not state that every martyr hears every".
blocks.text: It does not state that every martyr hears every caller, and it does not describe the condition or the location of the buried body. The reports examined below apply exactly this verse's language to al-Husayn ﵇ and then add hearing, recognition, and prayer.

blocks.observation: Framing who the believers of 9:105 are as the question the reports address; current text opens "Who "the believers" are, and what this seeing means".
blocks.text: Who "the believers" are, and what this seeing means after the Prophet's ﷺ death, is what the reports interpret.

blocks.observation: Report content that deeds are presented every morning, righteous and sinful; current text opens "The report has deeds presented to the Messenger ﷺ".
blocks.text: The report has deeds presented to the Messenger ﷺ every morning, the righteous and the sinful among them, and reads this as the meaning of Qur'an 9:105. The chains cite the Imams by their honorific names, Abu Abd Allah for al-Sadiq, Abu Ja'far for al-Baqir, and Abu Ja'far the Second, in one chain below, for al-Jawad. A second report on the same page describes his grief at the disobedience he sees among the deeds, and the grave instruction below addresses al-Husayn by his own kunya, Abu Abd Allah, the same name al-Sadiq carries in the chains.

blocks.observation: Basa'ir chapter heading naming presentation to the Imams living and dead; current text opens "Al-Saffar's Basa'ir al-Darajat gathers the same doctrine under a".
blocks.text: Al-Saffar's Basa'ir al-Darajat gathers the same doctrine under a chapter heading that names the dead Imams explicitly.

blocks.observation: Reading that the second report identifies the verse's believers as the Imams; current text opens "A second report of the al-Kafi chapter identifies "the".
blocks.text: A second report of the al-Kafi chapter identifies "the believers" of the verse as the Imams.

blocks.observation: Al-Rida prayer request report with the deeds-presentation reply; current text opens "A companion asks Imam al-Rida ﵇ to pray for".
blocks.text: A companion asks Imam al-Rida ﵇ to pray for him and his household and the report has the Imam answer with the doctrine and its verse reading.

blocks.observation: Synthesis that awareness of deeds is distinct from hearing every appeal; current text opens "Taken together, the verse and these reports support continued".
blocks.text: Taken together, the verse and these reports support continued awareness of what the living do. Awareness of deeds is not yet hearing of every spoken appeal; that further step comes from the grave reports, not from this verse.

blocks.observation: Introduction of the Sulayman story as answering a narrower objection; current text opens "The third passage answers a narrower objection, from the".
blocks.text: The third passage answers a narrower objection, from the story of Sulayman and the Queen of Saba's throne.

blocks.observation: What 27:40 establishes, granted extraordinary capacity with its limit stated; current text opens "The passage establishes that Allah can grant a servant".
blocks.text: The passage establishes that Allah can grant a servant an extraordinary capacity and that its use remains Allah's favour, not the servant's independent power. The man in the verse was alive. The verse does not establish action after death; it removes the assumption that no servant of Allah could ever be granted such a capacity at all.

blocks.observation: Section heading for the grave instruction; current text opens "## The Instruction at the Grave".
blocks.text: ## The Instruction at the Grave

blocks.observation: Placing the Uddat al-Da'i formula as the most direct text with its setting; current text opens "The most direct text is an instruction for a".
blocks.text: The most direct text is an instruction for a person with a need. Ibn Fahd al-Hilli records it in the fifth category of supplications, the category combined with a place.

blocks.observation: Analysis that the formula joins witness, life and request in one instruction; current text opens "The formula joins the three claims the question needs,".
blocks.text: The formula joins the three claims the question needs, witness, life in the words of Qur'an 3:169, and the request. The grant is sought from Allah; the Imam is asked to pray, not to grant. The limit is the chain. Ibn Fahd introduces the report with "it is reported from al-Sadiq ﵇" and prints no chain of transmission, isnad, at this locus, so the instruction cannot be presented as established, graded sahih, on this citation alone.

blocks.observation: The Mustadrak relay of the same instruction text; current text opens "Al-Nuri al-Tabrisi relays the same text with its setting.".
blocks.text: Al-Nuri al-Tabrisi relays the same text with its setting.

blocks.observation: What the relay confirms about the attribution and the later tradition; current text opens "The relay confirms the attribution as Ibn Fahd's book".
blocks.text: The relay confirms the attribution as Ibn Fahd's book transmits it and shows the later tradition reading it as an instruction to seek needs at the grave. It adds no independent chain.

blocks.observation: The following Uddat page's related al-Hadi report; current text opens "The following page of Uddat al-Da'i carries a related".
blocks.text: The following page of Uddat al-Da'i carries a related report in which an Imam speaks of his own future grave. A man cheated of his stipend asked Imam al-Hadi ﵇ to intercede, and the report has the Imam teach him a supplication instead. The extract prints only the closing words, al-Fath is a courtier of the story's caliph, and the supplication is the one the story has just taught.

blocks.observation: Reading that the Imam's words assume supplication used at a grave; current text opens "The Imam's own words as reported assume a supplication".
blocks.text: The Imam's own words as reported assume a supplication used at a grave after death and an answer from Allah; the inference rests on the wording, not on the chain's grade.

blocks.observation: The chained Ibn Uqda report naming both graves; current text opens "A report with a stated chain names both graves.".
blocks.text: A report with a stated chain names both graves.

blocks.observation: Identification of Ali and al-Husayn for the general reader; current text opens "Ali ﵇, the Prophet's cousin and son-in-law, and al-Husayn".
blocks.text: Ali ﵇, the Prophet's cousin and son-in-law, and al-Husayn ﵇, his grandson, are named after their deaths, called the martyrs who receive provision, the language of Qur'an 3:169 again, and the instruction is to visit them and turn there with one's needs. Ibn Tawus transmits the report with the same named route in Farhat al-Ghari (pp. 106-107), relaying it through Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Sa'id, who is Ibn Uqda. The Imam's us and you place the two graves among the visitor's people, not among his own. "Turn there with your needs" does not by itself specify whether one asks them to intercede or asks Allah at their graves. The Uddat al-Da'i formula supplies that specification, and it is the weaker attested of the two texts.

blocks.observation: The Kamil al-Ziyarat liturgy putting the request in the visitor's mouth; current text opens "The visitation liturgies put the same request in the".
blocks.text: The visitation liturgies put the same request in the visitor's mouth in plainer words.

blocks.observation: The Tahdhib ziyarah carrying the same structure; current text opens "Al-Tusi's Tahdhib al-Ahkam carries the ziyarah taught for the".
blocks.text: Al-Tusi's Tahdhib al-Ahkam carries the ziyarah taught for the grave with the same structure.

blocks.observation: Synthesis of the liturgies: addressed, heard, asked to intercede, Allah grants; current text opens "In these liturgies the Imam is addressed, heard in".
blocks.text: In these liturgies the Imam is addressed, heard in the sense the reports describe, and asked to intercede, and the visitor also seeks refuge in him and at his grave. Every effect the liturgies request is sought from Allah, and no text quoted gives the Imam an independent grant.

blocks.observation: Section heading for the seeing and acting reports; current text opens "## The Dead Who See and Act".
blocks.text: ## The Dead Who See and Act

blocks.observation: The longest al-Husayn report arising from a grave question; current text opens "The longest report describing al-Husayn ﵇ after his death".
blocks.text: The longest report describing al-Husayn ﵇ after his death comes from a question about his grave.

blocks.observation: Chain limit that both stated routes share al-Asamm before Ibn Bukayr; current text opens "Both stated routes pass through Abd Allah ibn Abd".
blocks.text: Both stated routes pass through Abd Allah ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Asamm before Ibn Bukayr, so the two chains are not independent confirmations of one another. The actions described are seeing, recognizing, and asking, and the forgiveness is sought from Allah.

blocks.observation: The longer Kamil version of the same scene; current text opens "Ibn Qulawayh transmits a longer version of the same".
blocks.text: Ibn Qulawayh transmits a longer version of the same scene.

blocks.observation: The added phrase answering what an opened grave would contain; current text opens "The added phrase answers the question Ibn Bukayr asked".
blocks.text: The added phrase answers the question Ibn Bukayr asked about the grave's contents, if it had been opened in his days he would have been found, and as for today he is alive with his Lord, and it belongs with the body texts below. This version also ends with the weeper returning with no sin upon him.

blocks.observation: The ordinary believer reports removing the exception assumption; current text opens "The corpus reports the same awareness for ordinary dead".
blocks.text: The corpus reports the same awareness for ordinary dead believers, which removes the assumption that this is a doctrine invented only for Imams.

blocks.observation: The al-Kafi chapter on the dead visiting their family; current text opens "The same volume of al-Kafi carries a chapter titled".
blocks.text: The same volume of al-Kafi carries a chapter titled "the dead person visits his family" (vol. 3, pp. 234-235). The believer visits his household in the form the reports describe, sees what pleases him, and some visit every Friday and some according to their deeds. Ali ﵇ instructs the living, in a route that again passes through al-Asamm.

blocks.observation: Placement of the Imam reports within the corpus's wider body; current text opens "The reports about the Prophet ﷺ and the Imams".
blocks.text: The reports about the Prophet ﷺ and the Imams ﵈ stand within the corpus's wider body of reports, not as an exception to it.

blocks.observation: The Basa'ir one-line principle report; current text opens "A report in Basa'ir al-Darajat has the Imam state".
blocks.text: A report in Basa'ir al-Darajat has the Imam state the principle in one line.

blocks.observation: The curtain scene of al-Hasan in the earlier report; current text opens "In the earlier scene it gives, al-Hasan ﵇ raised".
blocks.text: In the earlier scene it gives, al-Hasan ﵇ raised the curtain for a group of Shi'a after the killing of Ali ﵇, and the summary is Ali's own, whoever of us dies is not dead, and whoever remains of us is a proof against you. The chains also cite Abu al-Hasan, in the report on the dead believer's visits, for one of the later Imams; the chain does not print which. Seeing the deceased Imam is presented in the corpus as something that happened and as something the Imams ﵈ themselves taught about their own dead.

blocks.observation: Section heading for continuing knowledge; current text opens "## Knowledge That Keeps Arriving".
blocks.text: ## Knowledge That Keeps Arriving

blocks.observation: Statement that these are the corpus's strongest statements on continuing knowledge; current text opens "The reports on continuing knowledge are the corpus's strongest".
blocks.text: The reports on continuing knowledge are the corpus's strongest statements about the Prophet ﷺ and the Imams ﵈ after death. The reports call each Imam the wasi of the prophet before him, rendered in the translations variously as legatee, successor or executor and as trustee below, and they carry a scope distinction between the dead and the living trustee.

blocks.observation: Note on the first person plural of the living Imam speaking; current text opens "Here the words are the first person plural of".
blocks.text: Here the words are the first person plural of the living Imam speaking with all of them, our souls are not returned to our bodies except with newly acquired knowledge, and were it not so, what we have would run out. A third report, from al-Baqir to Zurara on the next page, says the same in the first person and makes the order of transmission explicit. The two reports together support the ascent, the worship, and the reception of knowledge, with the explicit increase wording resting on the living trustee's phrase.

blocks.observation: Statement of the strongest direct reports and their force; current text opens "These are the corpus's strongest direct reports that the".
blocks.text: These are the corpus's strongest direct reports that the Prophet ﷺ and the earlier Imams ﵈ continue to receive information after their deaths, and the knowledge is described as received from Allah and passed in order, not as self-originating.

blocks.observation: The Basa'ir chapter on acquired knowledge; current text opens "Basa'ir al-Darajat devotes a chapter to this acquired knowledge.".
blocks.text: Basa'ir al-Darajat devotes a chapter to this acquired knowledge.

blocks.observation: The chapter's reports on souls not returning except with a great matter; current text opens "The chapter's reports speak of their souls not returning".
blocks.text: The chapter's reports speak of their souls not returning to their bodies except with a great abundance of knowledge, in the same frame as al-Kafi's, and both routes pass through al-Hasan ibn Abbas ibn Huraysh, so they are one textual witness.

blocks.observation: Section heading for the body reports; current text opens "## Their Bodies, Raised or Preserved".
blocks.text: ## Their Bodies, Raised or Preserved

blocks.observation: Claim that the body reports divide and the corpus prints the division openly; current text opens "The reports on what happens to the body divide,".
blocks.text: The reports on what happens to the body divide, and the corpus prints the division openly.

blocks.observation: The clause that matters for visiting, that greetings reach them; current text opens "The clause that matters for the practice of visiting".
blocks.text: The clause that matters for the practice of visiting is the last one, greetings reach them from far away and they hear at the places of their traces from near. Al-Tusi transmits the same report with its own chain to the same teachers.

blocks.observation: The second report with the forty-day interval; current text opens "On the same page he transmits a second report".
blocks.text: On the same page he transmits a second report with a different interval.

blocks.observation: The three-versus-forty division printed by the same compiler; current text opens "Three days in one report, forty in another, both".
blocks.text: Three days in one report, forty in another, both printed by the same compiler with their chains. The page also carries the narrative of Ali's ﵇ burial.

blocks.observation: The Amali body-remaining side through al-Dizaj; current text opens "On the other side stand reports and arguments for".
blocks.text: On the other side stand reports and arguments for the body remaining. The Amali of al-Tusi transmits the account of the officer al-Mutawakkil sent to efface the grave.

blocks.observation: Al-Dizaj's two tellings, to the judge and to his servants; current text opens "Al-Dizaj tells the caliph's judge that he found nothing".
blocks.text: Al-Dizaj tells the caliph's judge that he found nothing and tells his servants the rest. Inside one report the public telling and the confidential one differ, and the corpus's body texts may diverge the same way. This report is one instance, not a rule.

blocks.observation: Jafar Murtada's survey of both groups of texts; current text opens "Sayyid Jafar Murtada al-Amili surveys both groups of texts".
blocks.text: Sayyid Jafar Murtada al-Amili surveys both groups of texts and the attempts to reconcile them.

blocks.observation: His position that the raising of the bodies is established; current text opens "His position is that the raising of the bodies".
blocks.text: His position is that the raising of the bodies is established, by the ascension of some prophets and by other texts, and that the reports of bodies remaining are then read as the deposited parts, the severed pieces, or the honour of the burial place. The next extract answers two reports his questioner had raised, a monk said to have kept a bone of a prophet, and al-Mufaddal's instruction to greet the bones of Adam, the body of Noah and the body of Ali. The reconciliation is his, and it is offered as an argument, not as a report. Qur'an 3:169 settles neither the location nor the condition of a martyr's buried body, and nothing in the practice of asking at a grave requires settling it. What the body texts do carry is the three-day report's own closing clause, that the greetings reach them from far away and are heard near the places of their traces.

blocks.observation: Section heading for appearances awake and in dreams; current text opens "## Seen Awake and in Dreams".
blocks.text: ## Seen Awake and in Dreams

blocks.observation: The awake encounters presented as a different class of evidence; current text opens "Several reports narrate encounters with the dead while awake,".
blocks.text: Several reports narrate encounters with the dead while awake, and they are a different class of evidence from dreams. The clearest is in al-Kafi.

blocks.observation: That the report mentions no dream and who Abu Bakr is; current text opens "The report mentions no dream. Abu Bakr here is".
blocks.text: The report mentions no dream. Abu Bakr here is the first caliph after the Prophet's death, and the command to repent of what is in his hand concerns the leadership he holds. The chain is a single route through Sahl ibn Ziyad and al-Hasan ibn al-Abbas ibn al-Jarish, left ungraded here. The account describes no grave opening and no body rising, so it is no proof about the buried body.

blocks.observation: The Basa'ir chapter on the Imams visiting the dead; current text opens "Basa'ir al-Darajat gathers such reports under a chapter title".
blocks.text: Basa'ir al-Darajat gathers such reports under a chapter title of its own, that the Imams ﵈ visit the dead and the dead visit them.

blocks.observation: The Quba account where the Prophet renders judgment; current text opens "In the Quba account the Prophet ﷺ renders judgment".
blocks.text: In the Quba account the Prophet ﷺ renders judgment against Abu Bakr, and the report itself records Umar's dismissal, the sorcery of Banu Hashim. Umar is the second caliph. The book carries several versions of the Quba scene on the following pages (pp. 296-299), one of them explicitly beginning from an unnamed transmitter, and several versions of one encounter are not several independent confirmations of it.

blocks.observation: The dream saying quoted inside the Amali dream narrative; current text opens "The dream saying of the Prophet ﷺ is quoted".
blocks.text: The dream saying of the Prophet ﷺ is quoted inside a dream narrative al-Tusi's Amali carries a few pages earlier, in which Abu Bakr ibn Ayyash, a Kufan Quran-reader of the generation after the Imams, a different man from the first caliph, dreams of al-Husayn's shrine at Karbala, its courtyard closed for the visitation of Abraham and Muhammad with Gabriel and Michael, and wakes to find the dream pointing him to the grave (pp. 353-354).

blocks.observation: The commander's deathbed account in the Amali; current text opens "The commander sent with al-Dizaj reports his deathbed account".
blocks.text: The commander sent with al-Dizaj reports his deathbed account in the Amali as well.

blocks.observation: The Kafi report identifying 10:64's good tidings as the dream; current text opens "A report in al-Kafi has the Prophet identify the".
blocks.text: A report in al-Kafi has the Prophet identify the good tidings of Qur'an 10:64 in the life of the world as the good dream.

blocks.observation: Each dream report standing on its own chain, the two classes separated; current text opens "A dream report narrates contact in a dream; each".
blocks.text: A dream report narrates contact in a dream; each stands on its own chain. Both classes presuppose what the waking reports state, that the dead are not absent. What a waking encounter adds over a dream is the dead present to the living; what the grave instructions add over both is the visitor's own address, attributed to the Imams, for the standing supplication at the grave.

blocks.observation: Section heading for the Sunni canon section; current text opens "## The Same Act in the Sunni Canon".
blocks.text: ## The Same Act in the Sunni Canon

blocks.observation: That the act the Shia reports describe appears in the Sunni canon too; current text opens "The reports above are Shia. The act they describe,".
blocks.text: The reports above are Shia. The act they describe, addressing a deceased Imam by name and seeking Allah through him, is carried by the Sunni canon as well, in texts its own scholars graded, and the Sunni form addresses the Prophet ﷺ himself. The report has him teaching it to a blind man.

blocks.observation: The blind man's instruction and the supplication's turn through the Prophet; current text opens "The blind man is told to perform ablution and".
blocks.text: The blind man is told to perform ablution and then make the supplication, whose turn is in the second person, I have turned through you to my Lord in this need of mine. Al-Tirmidhi's judgment follows the text, hasan sahih gharib, good, authentic and of a single route in his grading, known only through Abu Ja'far al-Khatmi. Al-Hakim transmits it through Abu Jafar al-Madani from Imarah ibn Khuzayma.

blocks.observation: Al-Hakim's sahih al-isnad grading following the text; current text opens "Al-Hakim's grading follows the text, sahih al-isnad, his formula".
blocks.text: Al-Hakim's grading follows the text, sahih al-isnad, his formula for an authentic chain in a report the two canonical collectors, al-Bukhari and Muslim, did not include. His version adds the vocative, O Muhammad, and the two units of prayer before the supplication. The form is an address to the Prophet ﷺ by name inside a prayer whose giver and grantor is Allah, the same structure the Shia visitation texts use.

blocks.observation: The continuation carrying the practice past the Prophet's death, documented; current text opens "The story's continuation carries the practice past the Prophet's".
blocks.text: The story's continuation carries the practice past the Prophet's ﷺ death, and it is documented in the Sunni hadith literature with its carriers named.

blocks.observation: Uthman ibn Hunayf teaching the same supplication after the death; current text opens "In the story, Uthman ibn Hunayf, the Companion who".
blocks.text: In the story, Uthman ibn Hunayf, the Companion who had witnessed the Prophet's ﷺ instruction, teaches a petitioner at the caliph Uthman ibn 'Affan's court the same supplication, with the Prophet ﷺ addressed by name after his death, and the need is met the same day. A second version in al-Hakim has the blind man himself healed on the spot.

blocks.observation: Ibn Hajar's assembly of the wider Sunni material; current text opens "Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani assembles the wider Sunni material in".
blocks.text: Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani assembles the wider Sunni material in Fath al-Bari.

blocks.observation: The blessings reaching him wherever the sender is; current text opens "The reports carry the blessings, salah, reaching him wherever".
blocks.text: The reports carry the blessings, salah, reaching him wherever the sender is, and the one who sends them upon him at his grave is heard by him. The Companions' question, how the blessings could reach him after his body had decayed, is answered in Ibn Kathir's version of the same report.

blocks.observation: The oldest form of seeking through the Prophet carried there; current text opens "The oldest form of seeking through the Prophet ﷺ".
blocks.text: The oldest form of seeking through the Prophet ﷺ is also carried there.

blocks.observation: Chain limit of two unnamed transmitters in the Adam report; current text opens "The report's chain, as printed, runs through two unnamed".
blocks.text: The report's chain, as printed, runs through two unnamed transmitters, a man of Kufa and a shaykh of Medina of the generation of Ibn Mas'ud's companions; it carries what the tradition itself transmits about the first supplication made through the Prophet ﷺ, before his creation in time as the reports frame it.

blocks.observation: Section heading for the hearing objection; current text opens "## The Hearing Objection".
blocks.text: ## The Hearing Objection

blocks.observation: The strongest objection beginning from the Qur'an's words to the Prophet; current text opens "The strongest objection of the practice's opponents begins from".
blocks.text: The strongest objection of the practice's opponents begins from the Qur'an's words to the Prophet ﷺ, that he does not make the dead hear (Qur'an 27:80), and that he cannot make those in the graves hear (Qur'an 35:22). The dead do not hear, therefore no request addressed to them can be received, and addressing them is an innovation that led Noah's people into shirk, the worship of others beside Allah. Ibn Taymiyya states the practical ruling.

blocks.observation: The shirk danger named as real while the texts are distinguished from it; current text opens "The danger his argument names, that grave-veneration opened the".
blocks.text: The danger his argument names, that grave-veneration opened the way to shirk, is real. The texts in evidence instruct the visitor to ask the dead Imam to pray to Allah, the act the Sunni canon carries in Tirmidhi's graded text and in the story of Uthman ibn Hunayf, and they do not instruct worship. The separate question, whether an address in this form already counts in its outward form as worship under the verses revealed about the idolaters of Mecca, is not settled here. On hearing itself, the Qur'an commentary (tafsir) of the objectors' own school limits what the proof text denies, and al-Shinqiti reads the parallel verse, 35:22, the same way (Adwa al-Bayan, vol. 6, p. 125).

blocks.observation: Al-Shinqiti's two sound readings and what the first denies; current text opens "Al-Shinqiti states that no reading of the verse is".
blocks.text: Al-Shinqiti states that no reading of the verse is sound except two. On the first, the dead of the verse are the disbelievers whose hearts Allah has killed, and the negated hearing is hearing that brings guidance and benefit. On the second, the negated hearing is the customary hearing from which the hearer benefits, and Ibn Taymiyya himself confined himself to this second reading. The second reading denies the dead only the hearing that benefits, and the first does not speak of the buried at all, since its dead are the living disbelievers. On the second the objection survives only as the claim that the dead lack beneficial hearing, and the canon's own reports of the buried hearing sandals and of the Prophet ﷺ hearing blessings at his grave are that school's answer. Abu Dawud's footsteps report and the blessings reports in Fath al-Bari are not contradictions to be explained away. They are what the canon itself affirms.

The dispute over this chain is a dispute inside the Sunni canon about one relay, not a finding that the practice lacks texts, and the gradings cited apply to the supplication itself.

blocks.text: The evidence supports the claim the clearest instruction makes. Al-Husayn ﵇, in the reports, hears the visitor who stands at his grave, knows him, prays to Allah for him, and can be asked to pray for his need. The Prophet ﷺ and the Imams ﵈, in the reports, are alive with their Lord, aware of the deeds of the living, and receiving knowledge that arrives from Allah. The reports do not give the dead independent power. The effects they seek are sought from Allah, by the prayer of the one addressed. The Sunni canon carries the same structure in texts its scholars graded. That removes the assumption that the practice was invented by the Shia against the rest of the tradition.

meta-and-process.evidence: The only method statements are the quotation convention and the closing chain-limits note; both carry fidelity content the reader needs, neither narrates process or history of revision.

decorative-contrast.evidence: The contrasts present are substantive and load-bearing, awareness versus hearing, addressed versus granting, awake versus dream; each carries a real distinction the argument needs, not decoration.

irony-and-theater.evidence: The objection section argues from quoted texts in plain declarative prose; no sarcasm, mockery, rhetorical questions or theatrical verdicts anywhere in the article.

openings-and-repetition.evidence: Every section opens with its content directly, a placed source or a stated claim; no announce-then-deliver scaffolding, and the conclusion states its result without ritually restating earlier sections.

paragraphs.text: 59 - (باب استحباب الاكثار من الدعاء وطلب الحوائج عند قبر الحسين (﵇)) (12149) 1 - أحمد بن فهد في عده الداعي : روي عن الصادق (﵇) : . من كانت له حاجة إلى الله عز ووجل ، فليقف عند رأس الحسين (﵇) وليقل : يا با عبد الله أشهد أنك تشهد مقامي وتسمع كلامي ، وأنك حي عند ربك ترزق ، فاسأل ربك وربي في قضاء حوائجي ، فإنها تقضى إن شاء الله تعالى .
59 - Chapter on the recommendation to make many supplications and seek one's needs at the grave of al-Husayn.

(12149) 1. Ahmad ibn Fahd, in Uddat al-Dai, narrated from al-Sadiq. Whoever has a need from God, Mighty and Majestic, let him stand at the head of al-Husayn and say, "O Abu Abd Allah, I bear witness that you witness my standing place and hear my words, and that you are alive and provided for by your Lord. So ask your Lord and my Lord concerning the fulfillment of my needs." They will be fulfilled, if God Most High wills.

paragraphs.text: قال ( ع ) : ان الفتح يوالينا بظاهره دون باطنه ، الدعا لمن دعا به بشرط ان يوالينا أهل البيت ، لكن هذا الدعا كثير اما ا دعو به عند الحوائج فتقضى ، وقد سئلت الله ﷿ ان لا يدعو به بعدى أحد عند قبري الا استجيب له

He said, "Al-Fath is allied with us outwardly but not inwardly. This supplication is for whoever supplicates with it, on condition that he be loyal to us, the People of the House. Yet this supplication is abundant. Whenever I supplicate with it in times of need, the needs are fulfilled. I have asked Allah that no one after me should supplicate with it at my grave without being answered."

paragraphs.text: 134 - ابن عقدة ، قال : حدّثنا حمّاد بن يعلى ، قال : أخبرني حسّان بن مهران الجمّال ، قال : قال لي جعفر بن محمّد : يا حسّان أتزور قبور الشهداء قبلكم ؟ قلت : أيّ الشهداء ؟ قال : عليّ وحسين . قلت : إنّا نزورهما فنكثر . قال : أولئك الشهداء المرزوقين ، فزوروهم وافزعوا عندهم بحوائجكم ، فلو يكونون منّا كموضعهم منكم لاتّخذناهم هجرة (2) .
134 - Ibn Uqda said, Hammad ibn Yala related to us. Hassan ibn Mihran al-Jammal told me that Jafar ibn Muhammad said to me, "O Hassan, do you visit the graves of the martyrs before you?"
I said, "Which martyrs?"
He said, "Ali and Husayn."
I said, "We visit them often."
He said, "Those are martyrs who are provided for. Visit them and turn there with your needs. If they were among us as they are among you, we would have made them a place of migration (2)."

paragraphs.text: يا أبا عبد الله يا حسين ابن رسول الله ، جئتك مستشفعا بك إلى الله ، اللهم إني أستشفع إليك بولد حبيبك ، وبالملائكة الذين يضجون عليه ويبكون ويصرخون ، لا يفترون ولا يسأمون ، وهم من خشيتك مشفقون ، ومن عذابك حذرون . لا تغيرهم الأيام ولا يهرمون ، في نواحي الحير يشهقون ، وسيدهم يرى ما يصنعون وما فيه يتقلبون ، قد انهملت (2) منهم العيون فلا ترقأ (3) ، واشتد منهم الحزن بحرقة لا تطفأ .

O Abu Abd Allah, O Husayn, son of the Messenger of God, I have come to you seeking your intercession with God. O God, I seek intercession from You through the child of Your Beloved, and through the angels who cry aloud over him, weep, and call out. They neither slacken nor grow weary. They are apprehensive out of fear of You and wary of Your punishment.

The days do not change them, nor do they grow old. In the precincts of al-Ha'ir they sob, and their master sees what they do and the state in which they turn. Tears have poured from their eyes and do not cease, and their grief has become intense with a burning that is not extinguished.

paragraphs.text: اللهم أبلغ روحه وجسده في ساعتي هذه وفي كل ساعة تحية مني كثيرة وسلاما ، آمنا بالله وحده واتبعنا الرسول فاكتبنا مع الشاهدين ، السلام عليك يا ابن رسول الله اتيتك بأبي أنت وأمي زائرا وافدا إليك متوجها بك إلى الله ربك وربي لينجح بك حوائجي ويعطيني بك سؤلي فاشفع لي عند ربك وكن لي شفيعا ، وقد جئتك هاربا من ذنوبي متنصلا إلى ربي من سئ عملي راجيا في موقفي هذا الخلاص من عقوبة ربي طامعا ان يستنقذني ربي بك من الردى ، اتيتك يا مولاي وافدا إليك إذ رغب عن زيارتك أهل الدنيا واليك كانت رحلتي ولك عبرتي وصرختي وعليك أسفي ولك نحيبي وزفرتي وعليك تحيتي وسلامي ، ألقيت رحلي بفنائك مستجيرا بك وبقبرك مما أخاف من عظيم جرمي واتيتك زائرا التمس ثبات القدم في الهجرة إليك ، وقد تيقنت ان الله ﷻ بكم ينفس الهم ، وبكم يكشف الكرب ، وبكم يباعدنا عن نائبات الزمان الكلب ، وبكم يفتح الله ، وبكم ينزل الغيث ، وبكم ينزل الرحمة ، وبكم يمسك الأرض ان تسيخ باهلها ، وبكم يثبت الله جبالها على مراسيها ، وقد توجهت إلى ربي يا سيدي في قضاء حوائجي ومغفرة ذنوبي فلا أخيبن من زوارك فقد خشيت ذلك أن لم تشفع لي ولا ينصرفن زوارك يا مولاي بالعطاء والحباء والخير والجزاء والمغفرة والرضا ، وانصرف انا مجبوها بذنوبي مردودا علي عملي فقد خيبت لما سلف مني ،

O God, convey to his spirit and body, at this hour of mine and at every hour, abundant greetings and peace from me. We have believed in God alone and followed the Messenger, so write us among the witnesses. Peace be upon you, O son of the Messenger of God. May my father and mother be your ransom. I have come to you as a visitor and arrival, turning through you to God, your Lord and my Lord, so that through you my needs may be fulfilled and He may grant me my request through you. Intercede for me with your Lord and be an intercessor for me.

I have come to you fleeing from my sins, renouncing my evil deeds before my Lord, hoping at this place where I stand for deliverance from the punishment of my Lord, and desiring that my Lord may rescue me through you from destruction. I have come to you, my master, arriving before you, when the people of this world have turned away from visiting you. My journey is to you, my tears and cry are for you, my sorrow is over you, and my wailing and sighing are for you. Upon you be my greeting and peace.

I have set down my baggage in your courtyard, seeking your protection and that of your grave from what I fear because of the enormity of my crime. I have come to you as a visitor, seeking firmness of foot in migrating to you. I have become certain that through you God relieves distress, through you He removes affliction, through you He keeps us far from the calamities of harsh time, through you God opens the way, through you He sends down rain, through you He sends down mercy, through you He holds the earth back from sinking with its inhabitants, and through you God secures its mountains upon their anchors.

I have turned to my Lord through you, my master, concerning the fulfillment of my needs and the forgiveness of my sins. Let me not be disappointed among your visitors, for I have feared that if you do not intercede for me, your visitors will depart, my master, with gifts, favors, goodness, recompense, forgiveness, and approval, while I return rebuffed because of my sins and my deeds are returned to me. I have indeed been disappointed because of what has preceded from me.

paragraphs.text: حدثني أبي ﵀ ، عن الحسين بن الحسن بن ابان ، عن الحسين بن سعيد ، عن عبد الله بن المغيرة ، عن عبد الله بن عبد الرحمان الأصم ، عن عبد الله بن بكير الأرجاني . وحدثني أبي ﵀ ، عن سعد بن عبد الله ، عن محمد بن الحسين ، عن محمد بن عبد الله بن زرارة ، عن عبد الله بن عبد الرحمان الأصم ، عن عبد الله بن بكير ، قال : حججت مع أبي عبد الله (﵇) - في حديث طويل - فقلت : يا بن رسول الله لو نبش قبر الحسين بن علي (﵉) هل كان يصاب في قبره شي ، فقال : يا بن بكير ما أعظم مسائلك ، ان الحسين (﵇) مع أبيه وأمه وأخيه في منزل رسول الله (﵌) ومعه يرزقون ويحبرون ، وانه لعن يمين العرش متعلق به يقول : يا رب أنجز لي ما وعدتني ، وانه لينظر إلى زواره وانه أعرف بهم وبأسمائهم وأسماء ابائهم وما في رحالهم من أحدهم بولده ، وانه لينظر إلى من يبكيه فيستغفر له ويسأل أباه الاستغفار له ويقول : أيها الباكي لو علمت ما أعد الله لك لفرحت أكثر مما حزنت وانه ليستغفر له من كل ذنب وخطيئة (2) .

My father related to me from al-Husayn ibn al-Hasan ibn Aban, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Abd Allah ibn al-Mughira, from Abd Allah ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Asamm, from Abd Allah ibn Bukayr al-Arjani. My father also related to me from Sa'd ibn Abd Allah, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Abd Allah ibn Zurara, from Abd Allah ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Asamm, from Abd Allah ibn Bukayr, who said,
"I made the pilgrimage with Abu Abd Allah, in a lengthy report. I said, 'Son of the Messenger of God, if the grave of al-Husayn ibn Ali were excavated, would anything be found in his grave?'

He said, 'O Ibn Bukayr, how grave your questions are. Al-Husayn is with his father, his mother, and his brother in the abode of the Messenger of God. With him they are provided for and made joyful. He is at the right of the Throne, clinging to it, saying, "My Lord, fulfill for me what You promised me." He looks upon those who visit him. He knows them, their names, the names of their fathers, and what is in their baggage better than any one of them knows his own child. He looks upon the one who weeps for him, asks forgiveness for him, asks his father to seek forgiveness for him, and says, "O you who weep, if you knew what God has prepared for you, you would rejoice more than you grieved." He seeks forgiveness for him for every sin and wrongdoing.'

Throne, saying, "My Lord, fulfill for me what You promised me."

He looks upon his visitors, and he knows them, their fathers' names, their ranks, and their standing before God better than any one of you knows his own child and what is in his saddlebag. He sees whoever weeps for him, so he seeks forgiveness for him out of mercy for him, and asks his father to seek forgiveness for him. He says, "O weeper, if you knew what has been prepared for you, you would rejoice more than you grieve." Everyone who hears his weeping among the angels in heaven and in al-Ha'ir seeks forgiveness for him. He returns with no sin upon him.

4 - Muhammad ibn Isa related to us from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Ammar ibn Marwan, from Sama'ah, who said,

"I entered upon Abu Abd Allah while I was speaking to myself. He noticed me and said, 'What is the matter with you, speaking to yourself? Do you wish to see Abu Ja'far?' I said, 'Yes.' He said, 'Rise and enter the house.' There was Abu Ja'far."

He said, "A group of the Shi'a came to al-Hasan ibn Ali after the killing of the Commander of the Faithful and asked him, 'Will you recognize the Commander of the Faithful when you see him?' They said, 'Yes.' He said, 'Then raise the curtain.' They raised it, and there was the Commander of the Faithful, whom they did not fail to recognize. The Commander of the Faithful said, 'Whoever of us dies does not die, and whoever of us remains is a proof against you.'"

"One day Abu Abd Allah said to me, though he had not previously addressed me by a kunyah, 'O Abu Abd Allah.'
I said, 'At your service.'
He said, 'Every Friday night we have joy.'
I said, 'May God increase you. What is that?'

paragraphs.text: 653 / 100 - أخبرنا ابن خشيش ، عن محمد بن عبد الله ، قال : حدثنا أحمد بن عبد الله بن محمد بن عمار الثقفي الكاتب ، قال . حدثنا علي بن محمد بن سليمان النوفلي ، عن أبي علي الحسين بن محمد بن مسلمة بن أبي عبيدة بن محمد بن عمار ابن ياسر ، قال : حدثني إبراهيم الديزج ، قال : بعثني المتوكل إلى كربلاء لتغيير قبر الحسين (﵇) ، وكتب معي إلى جعفر بن محمد بن عمار القاضي : أعلمك أني قد بعثت إبراهيم الديزج إلى كربلاء لنبش قبر الحسين ، فإذا قرأت كتابي فقف على الامر حتى تعرف فعل أو لم يفعل . قال الديزج : فعرفني جعفر بن محمد بن عمار ما كتب به إليه ، ففعلت ما أمرني به جعفر بن محمد بن عمار ثم أتيته ، فقال لي . ما صنعت ؟ فقلت : قد فعلت ما أمرت به ، فلم أر شيئا ولم أجد شيئا . فقال . لي : أفلا عمقته ؟ قلت : قد فعلت وما رأيت ، فكتب إلى السلطان : إن إبراهيم الديزج قد نبش فلم يجد شيئا وأمرته فمخره بالماء ، وكربه بالبقر . قال أبو علي العماري : فحدثني إبراهيم الديزج ، وسألته عن صورة الامر ، فقال لي . أتيت في خاصة غلماني فقط ، وإني نبشت فوجدت بارية جديدة وعليها بدن الحسين بن علي ووجدت منه رائحة المسك ، فتركت البارية على حالتها وبدن الحسين على البارية ، وأمرت بطرح التراب عليه ، وأطلقت عليه الماء ، وأمرت بالبقر لتمخره وتحرثه فلم تطأه البقر ، وكانت إذا جاءت إلى الموضع رجعت عنه ، فحلفت لغلماني بالله وبالايمان المغلظة لئن ذكر أحد هذا لأقتلنه .

653/100. Ibn Hashish informed us, from Muhammad ibn Abd Allah, from Ahmad ibn Abd Allah ibn Muhammad ibn Ammar al-Thaqafi the scribe, from Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Sulayman al-Nufali, from Abu Ali al-Husayn ibn Muhammad ibn Maslama, that Ibrahim al-Dizaj related to him, "Al-Mutawakkil sent me to Karbala to alter the grave of al-Husayn. He wrote with me to Jafar ibn Muhammad ibn Ammar, the judge, 'I inform you that I have sent Ibrahim al-Dizaj to Karbala to exhume the grave of al-Husayn. When you read my letter, attend to the matter until you know whether he has done it or not.'"

Al-Dizaj said, "Jafar ibn Muhammad ibn Ammar told me what had been written to him. I did what he ordered me to do, then I came to him. He said to me, 'What have you done?' I said, 'I have done what you ordered me to do. I saw nothing and found nothing.' He said to me, 'Did you not dig deeper?' I said, 'I did, and I saw nothing.' So he wrote to the ruler that Ibrahim al-Dizaj had exhumed it and found nothing, and that he had ordered him to let water run over it and plow it with cattle.

Abu Ali al-Amari said, "Ibrahim al-Dizaj related to me, and I asked him about how the matter had occurred. He said to me, 'I came with only my own slave boys. I exhumed it and found a new mat, with the body of al-Husayn ibn Ali upon it. I smelled musk from him. So I left the mat as it was and the body of al-Husayn upon the mat. I ordered earth to be thrown over it and released water over it. I ordered cattle to run over it and plow it, but the cattle would not tread upon it, and whenever they came to the spot, they turned back from it. I made my servants swear by God, with solemn oaths, that if any one of them mentioned this, I would kill him.'"

paragraphs.text: فإن رفع الأجساد إلى السماء ، ليس بالأمر الذي يصح التشكيك فيه ، بعد تصريح القرآن ، وتواتر الحديث به . . فإن معراج نبينا الأعظم بجسده وروحه ، ثابت بلا ريب ، وقد أشارت إليه آيات القرآن الكريم (1) . . والأحاديث الشريفة المتواترة . . وهذا دليل على الوقوع فضلاً عن الإمكان . . كما أن الله تعالى قد أشار إلى رفع النبي إدريس ﵇ ، إلى السماء (وَرَفَعْنَاهُ مَكَاناً عَلِيّاً) (2) . وقد صرحت الروايات بأن الله تعالى قد قبض روحه هناك (3) . . كما أن النبي عيسى ﵇ ، قد رفعه الله إليه ، كما صرحت به الآيات الكريمة . قال تعالى : (إِنِّي مُتَوَفِّيكَ وَرَافِعُكَ إِلَيَّ) وقال : (بَلْ رَفَعَهُ اللهُ إِلَيْهِ) (4) والروايات قد أكدت ذلك أيضاً (5) . .
The raising of bodies to heaven is not a matter that can properly be doubted after the Quran has stated it explicitly and reports about it have been transmitted through recurrent transmission.
The ascension of our greatest Prophet in body and spirit is established beyond doubt. The noble verses of the Quran have indicated it, as have the recurrent noble reports.
This is evidence of its occurrence, quite apart from its possibility.
God Most High has also indicated that He raised the Prophet Idris to heaven. "And We raised him to a high place." The reports have stated explicitly that God Most High took his soul there.

Likewise, God raised the Prophet Jesus to Himself, as the noble verses state explicitly. He Most High said, "I will take you in full and raise you to Me," and He said, "Rather, God raised him to Himself." The reports have also confirmed this.

paragraphs.text: وإذا كان الأمر كذلك ، فإن الحصول على هذا العظم لا يتناقض مع النصوص القائلة : إن أجساد الأنبياء لا تفنى ، فلعل الجسد باق ، وقد بقي معه ما دفن من أجزاء منفصلة عنه . . كالظفر ، والسن ، وما إلى ذلك . . بل إن الآيات القرآنية والأحاديث الشريفة قد دلت على أن المجرمين والطغاة كانوا يقتلون النبيين بغير حق ، وكانوا يقطعون أجسادهم بالمناشير . . فلعل هذا الجزء من ذلك الجسد الطاهر قد قطع ثم دفن . وهو لم يفن بعد . . حديث زيارة عظام آدم ويوسف : وأما بالنسبة لحديث المفضل بن عمر ، حول زيارة عظام النبي آدم ، وبدن النبي نوح ، وجسم الإمام علي ﵈ ، فنقول : أولاً : إن الحديث لا يصرح بموضع وجود تلك العظام ، وذلك البدن ، أو الجسد ، فلعلها رفعت في السماء ، لكن زيارتها في ذلك الموضع الذي كانت قد دفنت فيه توجب وصول السلام والزيارة إلى المزور عن قرب (1) ، لخصوصية في موضع الدفن . .

If this is so, then obtaining this bone does not conflict with the texts stating that the bodies of the prophets do not decay. Perhaps the body remains, along with what was buried with it of parts separated from it, such as a nail, a tooth, and the like.

Indeed, Quranic verses and noble reports indicate that criminals and tyrants used to kill the prophets unjustly and cut their bodies with saws. Perhaps this part of that pure body was cut off and then buried, and it has not yet decayed.
The report concerning the visitation of the bones of Adam and Joseph.
As for the report of al-Mufaddal ibn Umar concerning the visitation of the bones of the Prophet Adam, the body of the Prophet Noah, and the body of Imam Ali, we say the following.

First, the report does not state explicitly where those bones, that body, or that corporeal form are located. Perhaps they were raised to heaven, but visiting them at the place where they had been buried causes the greeting and visitation to reach the one visited nearby, due to a particular quality of the place of burial.

He said, "When I became familiar with him, I asked him about the blackness of his face, but he refused to tell me. Then he fell ill with the illness from which he died. I sat with him and asked him, and I saw that he wished to keep it concealed. So I guaranteed him secrecy, and he told me. He said, 'Al-Mutawakkil sent al-Dizaj and me to exhume the grave of al-Husayn and run water over it. When I resolved to depart and travel to that region, I saw the Messenger of God in a dream. He said, "Do not go out with al-Dizaj, and do not do what you have been ordered to do concerning the grave of al-Husayn."'

"When morning came, they came urging me to set out. I went with them until we reached Karbala, and we did what al-Mutawakkil had ordered us to do. I saw the Prophet in a dream, and he said, 'Did I not command you not to go out with them and not to do what they did? Yet you would not accept it until you did what they did.' Then he struck me across the face and spat in my face. My face became black as you see, while my body remained in its former condition."

paragraphs.text: 3578 - حَدَّثَنَا مَحْمُودُ بْنُ غَيْلَانَ قَالَ : حَدَّثَنَا عُثْمَانُ بْنُ عُمَرَ قَالَ : حَدَّثَنَا شُعْبَةُ ، عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ ، عَنْ عُمَارَةَ بْنِ خُزَيْمَةَ بْنِ ثَابِتٍ ، عَنْ عُثْمَانَ بْنِ حُنَيْفٍ ، أَنَّ رَجُلًا ضَرِيرَ البَصَرِ أَتَى النَّبِيَّ ﷺ فَقَالَ : ادْعُ اللَّهَ أَنْ يُعَافِيَنِي قَالَ : « إِنْ شِئْتَ دَعَوْتُ ، وَإِنْ شِئْتَ صَبَرْتَ فَهُوَ خَيْرٌ لَكَ » . قَالَ : فَادْعُهْ ، قَالَ : فَأَمَرَهُ أَنْ يَتَوَضَّأَ فَيُحْسِنَ وُضُوءَهُ وَيَدْعُوَ بِهَذَا الدُّعَاءِ : « اللَّهُمَّ إِنِّي أَسْأَلُكَ وَأَتَوَجَّهُ إِلَيْكَ بِنَبِيِّكَ مُحَمَّدٍ نَبِيِّ الرَّحْمَةِ ، إِنِّي تَوَجَّهْتُ بِكَ إِلَى رَبِّي فِي حَاجَتِي هَذِهِ لِتُقْضَى لِيَ ، اللَّهُمَّ فَشَفِّعْهُ فِيَّ » : هَذَا حَدِيثٌ حَسَنٌ صَحِيحٌ غَرِيبٌ لَا نَعْرِفُهُ إِلَّا مِنْ هَذَا الوَجْهِ مِنْ حَدِيثِ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ وَهُوَ الْخَطْمِي

3578 - Mahmud ibn Ghaylan related to us. Uthman ibn Umar related to us. Shu'bah related to us, from Abu Ja'far, from 'Umarah ibn Khuzaymah ibn Thabit, from Uthman ibn Hunayf, that a blind man came to the Prophet and said,
"Supplicate to Allah to grant me well-being."
He said, "If you wish, I will supplicate, and if you wish, be patient, for that is better for you."
He said, "Then supplicate to Him."

He said that he instructed him to perform ablution and do it well, then to supplicate with this supplication, "O Allah, I ask You and turn to You through Your Prophet Muhammad, the Prophet of mercy. I have turned through you to my Lord concerning this need of mine, so that it may be fulfilled for me. O Allah, accept his intercession for me."
This is a hadith that is hasan, sahih, gharib. We know it only through this route, from the hadith of Abu Ja'far, who is al-Khatmi.

Abu Ja'far al-Madani said, "I heard 'Umarah ibn Khuzaymah relate from Uthman ibn Hunayf that a blind man came to the Prophet and said, 'Supplicate to Allah Most High to grant me well-being.'"
He said, "If you wish, I will defer that, and if you wish, I will supplicate."
He said, "Then supplicate to Him."

He instructed him to perform ablution and do it well, to pray two units of prayer, and to supplicate with this supplication, "O Allah, I ask You and turn to You through Your Prophet Muhammad, the Prophet of mercy. O Muhammad, I turn through you to your Lord concerning this need of mine, so that He may fulfill it for me. O Allah, accept his intercession for me, and accept my intercession concerning him."
This hadith is sahih al-isnad; the two of them did not record it.

my Lord, so that He may fulfill my need for me,' and mention your need. Then go away until I come to you."

The man went and did that. Then he came to the door of Uthman ibn 'Affan. The doorkeeper came to him, took him by the hand, and brought him in to Uthman. He seated him with him on the carpet and said, "What is your need?"
He mentioned his need, and he fulfilled it for him. Then he said, "I did not understand your need until this very hour. Whenever you have a need, ask."
Then the man left him and met Uthman ibn Hunayf. He said to him, "May Allah reward you well. He would not consider my need or pay attention to me until you spoke to him."

Uthman ibn Hunayf said to him, "I neither spoke to him nor did he speak to me. But I witnessed the Messenger of Allah when a blind man came to him and complained to him of the loss of his sight. The Prophet said to him, 'Go to the place of ablution and perform ablution. Then go to the mosque and pray two units of prayer. Then say, "O Allah, I ask You and turn to You through Your Prophet, the Prophet of mercy. O Muhammad, I turn through you to my Lord, so that my sight may be uncovered for me. O Allah, accept his intercession for me, and accept my intercession for myself."'
Uthman said, "By Allah, we had not dispersed, nor had our conversation lasted long, before the man entered as though he had never had any impairment."

It was also related by al-Tirmidhi, al-Nasa'i, and Ibn Majah. Al-Tirmidhi said, "Sound, authentic, uncommon." Ahmad, Ibn Khuzaymah, and al-Hakim also related it, and he authenticated it, through 'Umarah ibn Khuzaymah ibn Thabit from Uthman ibn Hunayf, with similar wording. Allah knows best.

Abu Umamah ibn Sahl ibn Hunayf reported from his uncle, Uthman ibn Hunayf, that a man whose sight was impaired came to the Prophet and said, "Messenger of God, teach me a supplication by which I may call upon God to restore my sight." He said to him, "Say, 'O God, I ask You and turn to You through Your Prophet, the Prophet of mercy. O Muhammad, I have turned through you to my Lord. O God, accept his intercession for me, and accept my intercession for myself.'" He then made this supplication, rose, and was able to see.

paragraphs.text: ومن شواهد الحديث ما أخرجه أبو داود من حديث أبي هريرة رفعه وقال فيه وصلوا علي فان صلاتكم تبلغني حيث كنتم سنده صحيح وأخرجه أبو الشيخ في كتاب الثواب بسند جيد بلفظ من صلى على عند قبري سمعته ومن صلى علي نائيا بلغته وعند أبي داود والنسائي وصححه ابن خزيمة وغيره عن أوس بن أوس رفعه في فضل يوم الجمعة فأكثروا علي من الصلاة فيه فان صلاتكم معروضة علي قالوا يا رسول الله وكيف تعرض صلاتنا عليك وقد أرمت قال إن الله حرم على الأرض أن تأكل أجساد الأنبياء

Among the supporting reports for the hadith is what Abu Dawud recorded from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah, traced back to the Prophet. It includes, "Send blessings upon me, for your blessings reach me wherever you are." Its chain is authentic.

Abu al-Shaykh recorded in the Book of Reward, with a good chain, the wording, "Whoever sends blessings upon me at my grave, I hear it. Whoever sends blessings upon me from afar, it is conveyed to me."

Abu Dawud and al-Nasa'i recorded, and Ibn Khuzaymah and others authenticated, from Aws ibn Aws, traced back to the Prophet, concerning the merit of Friday, "Send abundant blessings upon me on it, for your blessings are presented to me."
They said, "O Messenger of Allah, how will our blessings be presented to you when you have decayed?"
He said, "Allah has forbidden the earth to consume the bodies of the prophets."

paragraphs.text: قال الإمام أحمد (2) : حدثنا حسين بن علي الجعفي عن عبد الرحمن بن يزيد بن جابر عن أبي الأشعث الصنعاني عن أوس الثقفي ﵁ قال : قال رسول اللّه ﷺ « من أفضل أيامكم يوم الجمعة ، فيه خلق آدم وفيه قبض ، وفيه النفخة ، وفيه الصعقة ، فأكثروا علي من الصلاة فيه ، فإن صلاتكم معروضة علي » قالوا : يا رسول اللّه ، وكيف تعرض عليك صلاتنا وقد أرمت ؟ يعني وقد بليت ، قال : « إن اللّه حرم على الأرض أن تأكل أجساد الأنبياء » (3) ورواه أبو داود والنسائي وابن ماجة من حديث حسين بن علي الجعفي ، وقد صحح هذا الحديث ابن خزيمة

Imam Ahmad said, "Husayn ibn 'Ali al-Ju'fi related to us, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Yazid ibn Jabir, from Abu al-Ash'ath al-San'ani, from Aws al-Thaqafi, who said that the Messenger of Allah said, 'Among your best days is Friday. On it Adam was created, on it he died, on it will be the blast, and on it will be the thunderclap. So send abundant blessings upon me on it, for your blessings are presented to me.'"
They said, "O Messenger of Allah, how will our blessings be presented to you when you have decayed?" Meaning, when you have become worn away.
He said, "Allah has forbidden the earth to consume the bodies of the prophets."
Abu Dawud, al-Nasa'i, and Ibn Majah also related it through the hadith of Husayn ibn 'Ali al-Ju'fi. Ibn Khuzaymah authenticated this hadith.

paragraphs.text: أخبرني رجل من أهل الكوفة من عباد الناس من الأنصار قال حدثني عبد الرحمن بن عبد ربه المازني من أهل البصرة عن شيخ من أهل المدينة من أصحاب عبد الله بن مسعود قال لما أصاب ادم الذنب نودي أن أخرج من جواري فخرج يمشي بين شجر الجنة فبدت عورته فجعل ينادي العفو العفو فإذا شجرة قد أخذت برأسه فظن أنها أمرت به فنادى بحق محمد ألا عفوت عني فخلي عنه ثم قيل له أتعرف محمدا قال نعم قيل وكيف قال لما نفخت في يا رب الروح رفعت رأسي إلى العرش فإذا فيه مكتوب محمد رسول الله (﵌) فعلمت أنك لم تخلق خلق أكرم عليك منه

A man from the people of Kufah, one of the devout worshippers among the Ansar, informed me. He said, "'Abd al-Rahman ibn 'Abd Rabbih al-Mazini, from the people of Basrah, related to me from an old man from the people of Madinah, who was among the companions of 'Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud.

When Adam committed the sin, he was called, 'Leave My vicinity.' So he went out, walking among the trees of Paradise, and his private parts became exposed. He began to call out, 'Pardon, pardon.' Then a tree caught hold of his head. He thought it had been commanded concerning him, so he called out, 'By the right of Muhammad, will You not pardon me?' So he was released.
Then he was asked, 'Do you know Muhammad?'
He said, 'Yes.'
It was said, 'How?'

He said, 'When, my Lord, You breathed the spirit into me, I raised my head to the Throne and found written upon it, "Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah." I knew that You had not created any creature more honored before You than he.'"

If this is forbidden, and it is a cause of the Lord's wrath and curse, then what of one who deliberately invokes the dead, supplicates at their graves and through them, and believes that this is among the means by which supplications are answered, requests are obtained, and needs are fulfilled?

This was among the first causes of shirk among the people of Noah and of the worship of idols among people. Ibn 'Abbas said, "There were ten generations between Adam and Noah, all of them upon Islam. Then shirk appeared because of their veneration of the graves of their righteous people."

paragraphs.text: الأول : أن المعنى : ( إِنَّكَ لاَ تُسْمِعُ الْمَوْتَى ) ، أي : لا تسمع الكفار الذين أمات اللَّه قلوبهم ، وكتب عليهم الشقاء في سابق علمه إسماع هدى وانتفاع ؛ لأن اللَّه كتب عليهم الشقاء ، فختم على قلوبهم ، وعلى سمعهم ، وجعل على قلوبهم الأكنة ، وفي آذانهم الوقر

The first is that the meaning of “Indeed, you cannot make the dead hear” is that you cannot make the disbelievers, whose hearts God has caused to die and upon whom He decreed wretchedness in His prior knowledge, hear in a way that brings guidance and benefit. For God decreed wretchedness for them, so He sealed their hearts and their hearing, and placed coverings over their hearts and heaviness in their ears.

paragraphs.text: فهكذا الموتى الذين ضرب بهم المثل لا يجب أن ينفى عنهم جميع أنواع السماع ، كما لم ينف ذلك عن الكفار ، بل قد انتفى عنهم السماع المعتاد الذين ينتفعون به ، وأمّا سماع آخر فلا ، وهذا التفسير الثاني جزم به واقتصر عليه أبو العباس ابن تيمية

Thus, the dead who were used in the comparison need not be denied every kind of hearing, just as that was not denied of the disbelievers. Rather, they have been denied the ordinary hearing by which they benefit. As for another kind of hearing, it has not been denied. Abu al-'Abbas Ibn Taymiyya stated this second interpretation decisively and confined himself to it.

I say that al-Nasa'i related it in the book Deeds of Day and Night through this route, from the hadith of Mu'adh ibn Hisham, from his father, from Abu Ja'far, from Abu Umamah Sahl ibn Hunayf, from his uncle Uthman ibn Hunayf.

He also related it from the hadith of Shu'bah and Hammad ibn Salamah, both from Abu Ja'far, from 'Umarah ibn Khuzaymah. None of these, neither al-Tirmidhi, al-Nasa'i, nor Ibn Majah, related through that uncommon route which contains the addition, the route of Shabib ibn Sa'id from Ruh ibn al-Qasim.
